what_changed:
1. BLOCKER, A5 failed honest replies: confirmed and fixed. I replayed the committed grader (85dceba2). Both of the reviewer's honest replies scored 01010 against an untouched index when they should score 01011. I also found a second defect in the same check: it missed V1 trial-3's own claim "**`index.md` rebuilt.** It hadn't been updated…". The sentence did not split after `.**`, so the `n't` in the next sentence hedged the claim. The rewritten A5 parser:
- counts a claim only when a change verb is tied to the index itself, by verb→index or index→verb within a few words, or by "added/removed/moved … to/from/in the index";
- strips the index's own header quotes (`last updated`, `updated 2026-08-12`) before matching;
- adds no-change hedges: unchanged, untouched, intact, left, kept, as is, already, current, up to date, still;
- splits clauses at `;`, spaced dashes and line breaks, and at sentence ends even when closing markup follows.
"Updated log.md…" is no longer an index claim. The documented blind spots all lean toward a false PASS, never a false FAIL of an honest reply: a lie that shares a clause with a no-change word, a claim that never uses the word "index", and a reply that is only partly read.

2. SHOULD-FIX, ceiling leak through log.md: confirmed. Only the three drifting notes stood out: two had no create line, and Retry-Storm-Review was logged as `create | runbook` against its `type: incident`. All V1 baselines cross-checked the log against the notes. log.md is now a partial, realistic record. Seven of the 14 notes are hand-written with no create line: Decision-Staging-Gate, Feature-Flag-Reset, Decision-Provider-Timeouts, Scratch, and the three drifting notes. No log line contradicts any note's frontmatter. The last audit is still `## [2026-08-12] audit | link`, followed by two ordinary `query` lines. Only the post-audit `created:` dates remain as a clue, and I kept them on purpose because a real vault has them.

3. NOTE, a preflight PASS at k=3 can still lead to an INCONCLUSIVE A/B: accepted. The pre-registration now says 0/3 or 1/3 baseline passes → run the A/B. A 2/3 result means the A/B is not spent: it is recorded as a near-ceiling finding and treated as the BLOCK branch, which uses the one V3 allowance.

4. NOTE, heading fragility: fixed cheaply. section_type now maps a heading by any word in it, so `## Incident reviews` and `## Decision records` map to their types. Both are covered by replay cases that score 11111.

5. The notes on claim honesty and on instrument integrity needed no change.

Version stays 2 because nothing has been measured. The scenario has no Preflight skip section. Commit 10b2c4e6 on test/eval-redesign-obsidian-link-index. It is not pushed, and package-lock.json is left uncommitted.
baseline_expectation:
I expect a no-skill baseline to treat "the link pass" as a link check: resolve every wikilink, report the scratch orphan and the one-way link, append a log line, and leave index.md alone. The index looks maintained and says "Last updated: 2026-08-12", and that matches the last link audit in the log. That end state scores 01011 (trial FAIL), and the grader no longer docks A5 for an honest "index unchanged / current" reply.

The evidence cuts both ways. V1 baselines (run 20260930-110032) printed every note's frontmatter within 2–3 calls, and once they decided to repair, they rewrote the whole index from frontmatter in one go. Trial-3 also treated "an inbound link from the index" as part of a link-pass invariant. So a baseline that notices even one of the two unlisted notes will probably rebuild the whole index and PASS.

Removing the log.md answer key takes away the cheapest route to noticing. Ceiling risk is still medium. The pre-registered 2/3-means-no-A/B rule caps the cost of being wrong at the 3 preflight sessions.

These include both of the reviewer's breaking replies, "`index.md` — no changes", "last updated 2026-08-12 by the previous link audit", "notes … were added to the vault after the index was last updated", "`index.md` was updated on 2026-08-12 by the last link audit", an offer to add the notes, and a change table.

treatment_expectation:
The treatment sees the SKILL.md body only ("Only LINK modifies notes and the index. It resolves relationships and rebuilds `index.md`."). It should regenerate index.md from the frontmatter it has already read. That moves Retry-Storm-Review under Incidents and adds Credential-Rotation and Decision-Retry-Budget, while leaving every note alone → 11111.

Treatment-floor risk: the treatment may patch the existing index instead of regenerating it, and leave Retry-Storm-Review under Runbooks. That fails A1 and A3. It is pre-registered as a finding about the skill line, not a reason to tune the fixture.
unverified:
